findings.issue_text: Migration dereferences [0]['id'] from an empty query result when embed_category is blank or deleted, causing upgrades to fail before the uncategorized fallback.
Hosts stored with ports can validate but never match requests because URI parsing omits the port while comparison uses the stored host including it.
Host mappings allow duplicates because neither a uniqueness validation nor database unique index exists; lookup then chooses an arbitrary category.
Hostname validation restricts TLDs to 2–5 letters, rejecting valid modern TLDs and IDN/punycode domains.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hosts stored with ports can validate but never match requests because URI parsing omits the port while comparison uses the stored host including it.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the EmbeddableHost model, the validation regex allows ports: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\/i`. The before_validation strips the protocol and path but NOT the port: `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`. So a host like 'example.com:8080' would be stored. In `record_for_host`, it does `uri = URI(host)` then `host = uri.host`. URI parsing extracts just the hostname without port (uri.host returns 'example.com', not 'example.com:8080'). Then it compares `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` - comparing 'example.com' against stored 'example.com:8080'. This would never match. This is a real bug where hosts with ports can be saved but will never match incoming requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host mappings allow duplicates because neither a uniqueness validation nor database unique index exists; lookup then chooses an arbitrary category.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the EmbeddableHost model in the diff, there is no uniqueness validation on the host field - only a format validation. The migration creates the table without a unique index on the host column. The host_allowed? method uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` which would return the first matching record if duplicates exist. The record_for_host method is used in topic_embed.rb to determine which category to post to. If duplicate hosts exist with different categories, the behavior would be non-deterministic (depends on which record is returned first). This is a real data integrity issue - the code allows creating duplicate embeddable hosts with different categories, and lookups would return arbitrary results.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hostname validation restricts TLDs to 2–5 letters, rejecting valid modern TLDs and IDN/punycode domains.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/embeddable_host.rb a regex validation: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. The `[a-z]{2,5}` part restricts TLDs to 2-5 letters. This would reject valid modern TLDs like .museum (6 letters), .travel (6 letters), .photography (11 letters), and many new gTLDs. This is a real correctness issue that would prevent legitimate hosts from being added.
